description: Accelerating the National QR Payments Adoption
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-03-23 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Government has identified the promotion of the digital economy as a national priority to enhance economic efficiency, financial inclusion and financial transparency. Cash is heavily used for everyday retail transactions in the country, whereby transparency and the growth of the digital economy have been limited. Although the LankaQR infrastructure is currently operational with over 20 financial institutions and nearly 30 mobile applications, their active use is relatively low. During the third quarter of 2025, approximately 274,000 transactions were recorded through LankaQR, with a total value of about Rs.1.18 billion. This works out to an average of about 90,000 transactions per month, with a value of about Rs. 390 million. Accordingly, it is observed that the value of an average transaction made through QR code is less than Rs.5,000/. The proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Digital Economy, to implement a programme for promoting digital payments based on QR codes without charging any additional fees to both the sender and the recipient for transactions below Rs.5,000/- taking into consideration the above matters and in line with the proposal presented in the 2026 Budget in this regard, was approved by the Cabinet.
